transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Hi Dr. Smith. I'm here because I've been making a lot of careless mistakes lately and really struggle to pay attention to details, especially at work. It's getting to the point where it's causing some real problems for me.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in activities you used to enjoy, or are these attention issues mainly accompanied by a lot of worrying thoughts?
No, I haven't really been feeling down or worrying excessively about things. My struggles are mostly just with keeping my attention focused and dealing with this constant feeling of restlessness.
When you say restlessness, do you mean an inner sense of fidgeting or an actual need to move around, like tapping, squirming, or getting up frequently?
It’s really a mix of both for me. I have a constant inner sense of restlessness, but I also frequently feel a strong physical urge to get up and leave my seat, even when I'm expected to stay seated.

{
  "category": "differential point",
  "subcategory": "duration, onset",
  "question": "When did these symptoms first start, and have they been present since childhood or did they begin more recently?"

This current stretch of constant symptoms has been going on for about a year now. But looking back, I actually first started experiencing these exact same difficulties during childhood, well before I turned 12.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidate was only Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation), and it remains the sole candidate. The patient reports childhood onset of symptoms (before age 12), persistent duration (current episode lasting about a year but with lifelong history), and both inattention (careless mistakes, difficulty sustaining attention) and hyperactive/impulsive symptoms (inner restlessness, physical urge to leave seat). These are core diagnostic criteria for ADHD, and the combined presentation is supported by the presence of both symptom domains. No symptoms suggestive of mood, anxiety, psychotic, or other psychiatric disorders were endorsed, so no other candidates have been added.
